chunks: 897 - Abu Bakr al-Haḍramī and Kulayb al-Asadī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he recited the adhan for them and said:

"Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. Come to the best of deeds, come to the best of deeds. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah, there is no god but Allah."

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; a declaration of testimony
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: the establishment call before beginning the prayer
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ: come to the best of deeds

ai.seo_question: What is the wording of the adhan and iqamah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits the wording of the adhan as taught by Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, including the phrase ḥayya ʿalā khayri al-ʿamal. It also states that the iqamah is the same, indicating a jurisprudential teaching on the form of the call and establishment of prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.897 - Abu Bakr al-Hadhrami and Kulaib al-Asadi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that he taught them the adhan, saying:

"Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar (Allah (swt) is the Greatest, repeated four times).
I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt) (twice).
I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (sw) (twice).
Hasten to prayer (twice).
Hasten to success (twice).
Hasten to the best of deeds (twice).
Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. There is no god but Allah (swt) (twice)."
